notes: Linux only: on Windows both runtimes skip TestSymVersion identically (skipIfNotELF), so the Windows row stays 10 matched / 0 disclosed and this entry never fires there.

disclosures.name: TestSymVersion
disclosures.reason: Host identity, reached through Go's own skip. TestSymVersion -> getTable -> crack(os.Args[0]) -> parse, whose first act is `if f.Section(".gosymtab") == nil { t.Skip("no .gosymtab section") }`: it cracks the running test binary. On Linux, Go's test binary is a Go ELF with a .gosymtab section, so the Go side passes; the converted host is a .NET apphost with no Go symbol table, so the same upstream guard fires and the converted side skips with Go's own text. Nothing in the package is wrong, and nothing go2cs owns can satisfy it short of shipping a Go pclntab inside a .NET executable.
